questions.title: How does the Lead edit a document live, and what is 'Wordcraft'?
questions.context: Your Q10 note: the Lead should live-edit the document, and each researcher decides whether its changes arrive as comments or as direct rewrites. Today every Lead edit is a proposal a person accepts, and your auto-accept toggle accepts text edits automatically. 'Wordcraft' isn't defined anywhere in the plans: if you mean a specific product or editor, name it in the note. I've assumed this covers the study context file and the report (Q6's free report edits).
questions.example: Jana opens the report's Interpretace section with her Lead. Under (a), with her setting on 'Návrhy', the Lead's rewrite shows as tracked changes she accepts or rejects one by one. Petr has 'Přímé úpravy' on: the Lead rewrites the paragraph in place, it's marked 'upraveno Vedoucím', and he can undo it. Either way the numbers stay ledger references.

options.label: Per researcher: suggestions or direct edits
options.detail: Tracked-change suggestions by default; a researcher can switch to direct, undoable rewrites. Extends the auto-accept toggle; numbers stay ledger references

options.label: Direct edits only
options.detail: The Lead always rewrites in place; the researcher undoes

options.label: Proposals only in the MVP
options.detail: Keep accept/dismiss; live co-editing after the MVP

questions.rationale: It is what your note describes, and it builds on the toggle and edit gate that already exist. Suggestions as the default keep a person's eyes on every change unless they choose otherwise.
